newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BARGAIN HUNTERS EMERGE, BUT BRUSSELS BOURSE WARY.
newsitem.headline: BARGAIN HUNTERS EMERGE, BUT BRUSSELS BOURSE WARY.

text.p: Bargain hunters came off the sidelines to pick up selected stocks on Monday, but their activities did little to help a Brussels bourse pushed lower by Wall Street, the dollar and fear of rising interest rates.
"At these very low levels we have seen bargain hunters for stocks such as Bekaert, Kredietbank, Colruyt and Quick," one trader said.

"We opened much lower, but that may prove to have been the low point of the day. The market will wait now to see what U.S. bonds and the dollar do. That and the possibility of a German rate rise hold the key to the future," he added.
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares .BFX, which opened 1.6 percent down, was 0.9 percent off at 2,408.68 at 0915 GMT, with 12 issues lower, four unchanged and four higher.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, which at one stage dropped to 24,000 francs, was at 24,475 -- down 525 from Friday's close.
Kredietbank was at 14,625 francs after falling to 14,400, while retailer Colruyt was at 17,550 from an earlier 17,100. Both were still below their Friday closes.
Hamburger chain Quick edged above Friday's close at 2,090 francs after initially falling to 2,000 francs.
Quick jumped more than 10 percent early last week on a 'buy' recommendation from Bank Delen, but then dropped back on profit-taking and 'sell' recommendations from other brokers.
Specialty chemicals firm Tessenderlo was the main loser on the Brussels bourse, down 3.6 percent at 1,850 francs.
Dollar-sensitives such as chemicals and drugs firm UCB and retailer Delhaize were off 2.3 and 2.1 percent respectively.
On the plus side, construction firm Franki continued its steady rise, climbing 3.7 percent to 498 francs -- although only on the basis of one move.
